title: ChoiceDialog
summary: The standard confirmation dialog: a title, an optional message and one button per option, plus Cancel. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: When an action needs the person to pick one of a few named options before it runs. Each option is a button whose title says what it does; Cancel only ever means do nothing.
whenNotToUse: For more than about five options, or options that need descriptions, present a sheet with a list or a Picker. For a yes or no on a destructive action see confirm-dialog.
api: func confirmationDialog(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
Button(_ title: String, role: ButtonRole?, action: () -> Void)

states.name: presented on iPhone
states.description: An action sheet rises from the bottom, with Cancel separated below the options.

states.name: presented on iPad
states.description: A popover anchored to the view the modifier is on; tapping outside cancels.

appearance: The system draws the dialog in every theme, following the light or dark appearance. A destructive option is the system's red. Monarch does not colour the buttons.
platformNotes: The web ChoiceDialog shows radio cards with descriptions and tones, then a Confirm button, and has pending and error states and a promise API. The system dialog runs an option's action the moment it is tapped, so there is no separate confirm step, no description per option, no disabled option and no pending state: show progress and errors on the screen that asked, after the dialog closes. For options that need descriptions, build a sheet. Android uses a Material dialog with radio rows.
accessibility: System behaviour: the dialog is modal; VoiceOver focus moves into it and returns to the presenting control when it closes.
System behaviour: the title and message are read first, then each option as a button.
System behaviour: the escape gesture and tapping outside choose Cancel.
Write option titles that make sense on their own, without the question.
edgeCases: The title is hidden on iPhone unless titleVisibility is .visible.
Without a button with the cancel role the system adds its own Cancel on iPhone.
Buttons in the dialog cannot be styled; only roles are honoured.
